docs/README.md::project-overview

Project Overview

Project Overview

Baselayer is an offline, DAG-routed documentation workspace for agentic coding. Two surfaces compile from one canonical graph (.context/graph.json):

| Surface | Purpose | Audience | |---------|---------|----------| | Agent router (AGENTS.md + .context/manifest.json) | Token-efficient routing for AI agents | Models | | Human wiki (.wiki/index.html) | Offline HTML wiki with full prose | People |

docs/README.md::architecture

Architecture

Architecture

The workspace consists of the baselayer (docs → graph → manifest + wiki) plus the Unified Prompt Stack (prompt DAG, compiler, adapters, provenance, wiki views) layered on top.

docs/README.md::conventions

Conventions

Conventions

- docs/ is read-only to the build; graph.json is the only writable knowledge file — edit docs or graph, then rebuild. - Skills are one folder per name, SKILL.md frontmatter authoritative; descriptions are load-bearing (progressive disclosure Layer 1). - Secrets live only in .agent/.env (gitignored); .env.example is the committed template. - The master library (3,520 skills) is categorized in .agent/skills/CATEGORIZATION.md; the 47 broken sources are quarantined in IMPORT_REPORT.md; bulk-installing is prohibited. - Secrets: docs/operations/secrets.md — key storage, rotation, leak response.

docs/README.md::validation-rules-validate-py

Validation Rules (validate.py)

Validation Rules (validate.py)

1. Graph integrity: All node byte_range valid, sha256 matches content 2. Manifest consistency: Every node in manifest exists in graph, edges valid 3. Router budget: manifest.json < 15% of context window (~1,400 tokens) 4. Skill index: skills/index.json matches .harness/skills/ contents 5. Wiki generation: .wiki/index.html builds without error 6. No generated files modified: Manifest, wiki, index.json not hand-edited

docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md::adr-001-why-a-dag-for-documentation-routing

ADR-001: Why a DAG for Documentation Routing

ADR-001: Why a DAG for Documentation Routing

docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md::status

Status

Status

Accepted

requires

doc docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md

docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md::context

Context

Context

The baselayer workspace needs a documentation system that serves two audiences: - Humans who need an explorable, cross-linked wiki - AI agents who need a token-efficient router that surfaces only relevant sections

A flat directory of Markdown files doesn't scale: agents can't tell which sections are relevant without reading everything, and humans can't navigate cross-references without manual link maintenance.

A graph database would be powerful but adds dependencies and operational complexity. A simple index file loses the structural relationships between sections.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md

docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md::decision

Decision

Decision

Use a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) where: - Nodes are documentation sections (one per Markdown heading), identified by path::slug - Edges are requires relationships between sections - Byte ranges pin each node to an exact slice of its source file - SHA-256 hashes verify content integrity

The graph is compiled from docs/ by seed.py, then rendered to manifest.json (agent router) and .wiki/index.html (human wiki) by build.py.

doc docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md

docs/adr/ADR-001-dag-routing.md::consequences

Consequences

Consequences

Positive: - Agents read only relevant sections (byte-range hydration), keeping router under ~15% of context budget - Humans get an explorable, cross-linked wiki with search - Content integrity verified via SHA-256 on every build - DAG acyclicity enforced at build time — no circular references

Negative: - Adding a new section requires editing docs/ then rebuilding (not live-editing the graph) - Edge relationships are manual (declared in manifest edges, not auto-discovered) - The DAG is a compile-time artifact, not a runtime query engine

docs/adr/ADR-002-byte-ranges.md::context

Context

Context

The baselayer indexes docs/ Markdown files at the section level (one node per heading). Two approaches were considered:

1. File-level indexing: Each .md file is one node. Agents must read entire files to find relevant content. 2. Section-level indexing: Each heading-delimited section is one node with a byte_range pinpointing its exact location in the file.

File-level indexing wastes tokens: an agent looking for one configuration detail must read the whole file. Section-level indexing enables token-efficient hydration but requires precise byte tracking.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/adr/ADR-002-byte-ranges.md

docs/adr/ADR-002-byte-ranges.md::decision

Decision

Decision

Use section-level indexing with byte_range: [start, end] in every manifest node. The seed.py compiler scans each Markdown file, identifies heading lines via regex, and computes exact byte offsets. The build.py compiler validates that each byte range's SHA-256 matches the content at that slice.

Agents hydrate sections by reading exactly content_ref bytes [start:end] — never the whole file.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/adr/ADR-002-byte-ranges.md

docs/adr/ADR-002-byte-ranges.md::consequences

Consequences

Consequences

Positive: - Token-efficient: agents read only relevant sections - Content integrity: SHA-256 on byte slice detects any drift - Progressive disclosure: frontmatter (~50-100 tokens) always loaded, body on demand - Router stays under ~15% of context budget (~1,400-10,000 tokens depending on corpus size)

Negative: - Byte ranges break if file content shifts (sections insert/delete lines) — requires rebuild - No live editing of individual sections without re-indexing - Slightly more complex compiler (must track byte positions during scan)

docs/adr/ADR-003-stdlib-only.md::context

Context

Context

The baselayer tooling (seed.py, build.py, validate.py, and all tools/) runs in the AndroidHarness environment (Android 17, API 37, app UID). Three dependency options were considered:

1. pip install: Requires network access, package management, and potential compilation of native extensions. Not always available in the Android/Termux environment. 2. Vendored dependencies: Bundling third-party packages in the repo increases size and creates supply-chain concerns. 3. Standard library only: Uses only Python 3.14 stdlib modules. Zero dependencies, zero network, zero compilation.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/adr/ADR-003-stdlib-only.md

docs/adr/ADR-003-stdlib-only.md::decision

Decision

Decision

All baselayer tooling uses Python 3 standard library only. No pip install of any kind. Tools that need HTTP (e.g., check_links.py) use urllib.request. Tools that need hashing use hashlib. Tools that need JSON use json.

requires
none
required by

doc docs/adr/ADR-003-stdlib-only.md

docs/adr/ADR-003-stdlib-only.md::consequences

Consequences

Consequences

Positive: - Zero network required — works fully offline - Zero installation — runs on any Python 3.14+ system - No supply-chain attacks via compromised packages - Predictable behavior across environments - Smaller repo (no vendored packages)

Negative: - More verbose code for common tasks (e.g., HTTP, argument parsing) - Some modern Python features unavailable (but 3.14 is quite complete) - Cannot use rich ecosystem (requests, click, pyyaml, etc.)

docs/adr/ADR-004-agent-tracked.md::context

Context

Context

The .agent/ directory holds the master skill library (3,520 skills), agent profiles, tools, MCP server, and machine registry. Two deployment models were considered:

Model A (tracked): .agent/ is source-controlled. Only .agent/.env (secrets) and .agent/.harness/ (provisioned snapshot) are gitignored.

Model B (untracked): .agent/ is provisioned by bootstrap on each clone. Only .agent/README.md and .agent/.env.example are tracked via negation rules.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/adr/ADR-004-agent-tracked.md

docs/adr/ADR-004-agent-tracked.md::decision

Decision

Decision

Model A (tracked). The full master skill library is committed to git. Rationale:

- Source of truth: .agent/skills/ is the canonical library; tracking it enables history, review, and reproducible provisioning - Auditability: Skill curation (add/edit/quarantine) is auditable via git log - Reproducibility: Same commit → same active skill set - Already committed: 12,000+ files already in the repository; switching to Model B would lose history

Model B would be better for very large libraries (>50K skills) or when skills are fetched from external registries, but neither applies here.

none

doc docs/adr/ADR-004-agent-tracked.md

docs/adr/ADR-004-agent-tracked.md::consequences

Consequences

Consequences

Positive: - Git history for all skill changes - Reproducible skill provisioning from any commit - Pre-commit validation on skill changes - Easy to review skill additions/modifications

Negative: - Large repo size (12,000+ skill files) - .agent/.env must be carefully gitignored to prevent secret leaks - Clone/download time is larger than Model B

docs/adr/ADR-005-audit-findings.md::phase-1-changes-implemented-complete

Phase 1 Changes Implemented (COMPLETE)

Phase 1 Changes Implemented (COMPLETE)

1. Graph schema versioning — Added schema_version: "1.0.0" to graph.json (seed.py) and propagated to manifest.json (build.py). 2. Byte range validation — build.py and validate.py now check: start >= 0, end > start, end <= file size. 3. Structured logging — seed.py, build.py, validate.py, MCP server.py use logging module with INFO/WARNING/ERROR severity to stderr. 4. Graceful malformed input — seed.py skips symlinks, files > 10MB, and binary files (null byte check) with WARNING logs. 5. MCP server hardening — Added structured logging, request metrics (count, latency, token bytes, verification failures, errors), per-call SHA-256 verification on read_section, graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT, health check (ping returns structured status). 6. MCP integration tests — tests/test_mcp.py with 9 tests covering ping, tools/list, read_section (verified + unknown node), compile_context, search_nodes, list_nodes, unknown tool, invalid JSON. 7. CI workflow — .github/workflows/ci.yml runs unit tests, build pipeline, skill audit, build determinism check, .env-not-committed check, pre-commit hook executable check, Python syntax linting.

docs/architecture.md::dag-compiler-stages

DAG Compiler Stages

DAG Compiler Stages

1. Scope resolution — Incoming delegation envelope carries task_type, domain, allowed_targets, target_tier. These are root selectors. 2. Graph traversal — Starting from the selected Envelope node, walk requires, triggers, and routes_to edges. Select only nodes whose conditions match scope. 3. Budget-aware ordering — Topologically sort selected nodes, then assign token budgets per layer. If total exceeds per-tier ceiling, prune nodes by edge distance from root (farthest triggers nodes dropped first). Never silently truncate; return BLOCKED with excluded node IDs. 4. Cache-keyed rendering — Render frozen prefix from SystemPrompt node + Adapter. Render variable suffix from remaining nodes in dependency order. Append suffix after prefix.

docs/contracts/decisions/Q1-rpo-rto.md::context

Context

Context

The audit persistence spec requires configurable retention and durability guarantees. We need to define Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) targets that balance data safety with performance.

doc docs/contracts/decisions/Q1-rpo-rto.md

docs/contracts/decisions/Q1-rpo-rto.md::options-considered

Options Considered

Options Considered

| Option | RPO | RTO | Write Latency | Durability | |--------|-----|-----|---------------|------------| | A: Sync on every write (fsync) | 0 | < 1s | ~10-50ms | Maximum | | B: Batch fsync every 100ms | ≤ 100ms | < 5s | ~1-5ms | High | | C: Async with WAL checkpoint | ≤ 1s | < 30s | ~0.5ms | Standard | | D: Application-level checkpoint | Configurable | Configurable | ~0.1ms | Tunable |

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/contracts/decisions/Q1-rpo-rto.md

docs/contracts/decisions/Q1-rpo-rto.md::decision

Decision

Decision

Option A (Sync on every write) for the primary SQLite store.

Rationale: - Audit trail is immutable by design — any loss is unacceptable - Write volume is low (≈10-50 records/session), so latency cost is negligible - WAL mode + PRAGMA synchronous=FULL provides crash consistency without application complexity - JSONL secondary export provides additional durability layer

SQLite's PRAGMA synchronous setting controls durability vs performance trade-off. The audit persistence spec requires choosing between FULL (maximum durability) and NORMAL (balanced). This decision documents benchmark results.

docs/contracts/decisions/Q2-sqlite-sync.md::key-observations

Key Observations

Key Observations

1. FULL p99 (8.2ms) well within 10ms target — meets spec requirement 2. Read performance identical across modes (WAL reads don't sync) 3. NORMAL risk: On Android, power loss during checkpoint can corrupt WAL → database unrecoverable 4. OFF unacceptable: Any audit loss violates immutability requirement

doc docs/contracts/decisions/Q2-sqlite-sync.md

docs/contracts/decisions/Q2-sqlite-sync.md::decision

Decision

Decision

Use PRAGMA synchronous=FULL for the audit database.

Rationale: - p99 write latency (8.2ms) < 10ms target with 20% margin - Zero data loss on crash/power loss — required for immutable audit trail - Read performance unaffected - Simpler than application-level durability logic

docs/contracts/decisions/Q4-skill-categorization-stability.md::rationale

Rationale

Rationale

The categorization schema is a contract between the master library and the provisioning pipeline. Downstream consumers (provisioning, skill picker, index generator, audit tool) read the CSV by column name. Industry practice for such contracts:

1. Additive changes are safe — new enum values don't break readers 2. Renames/removals are breaking — readers reference values by string 3. Versioning signals intent — major version = breaking change, minor = additive 4. Migration tooling required for breaking changes — not optional

This mirrors semantic versioning for data contracts (cf. Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema evolution rules).

docs/contracts/decisions/Q5-wiki-render-pipeline.md::evidence

Evidence

Evidence

- Current seed.py: walks docs/, parses every .md, extracts sections, writes graph.json (83 nodes, ~15KB) - Current build.py: reads graph.json, generates manifest.json + wiki/index.html (~88KB) - Full rebuild time: ~0.7s total (seed: 0.3s, build: 0.4s) on Android 17 device - docs/ size: ~15 files, ~15KB total markdown - No external dependencies; pure Python 3.14 stdlib - validate.py validates entire graph/manifest/wiki consistency

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/contracts/decisions/Q5-wiki-render-pipeline.md

docs/contracts/decisions/Q5-wiki-render-pipeline.md::rationale

Rationale

Rationale

Industry baselines for static site generators and documentation pipelines:

| Approach | Examples | Trade-off | |----------|----------|-----------| | Full rebuild | Sphinx, MkDocs (default), Hugo, Jekyll | Simple, correct, fast enough for small corpora | | Incremental | VitePress, Next.js, Astro | Complex cache invalidation, risk of stale output | | Hybrid | MkDocs --dirtyreload, Sphinx -j auto | Opt-in, development only |

For our corpus (15 files, <1s rebuild), full rebuild is correct by default. The complexity of incremental (file watching, hash tracking, partial graph merge, partial HTML rewrite) is not justified. Incremental can be added later as --incremental flag using SHA-256 content hashes already stored in graph.json nodes.

Key principle: Correctness over speed for the canonical pipeline. The build is fast enough that incremental optimization is premature.

doc docs/contracts/decisions/Q6-profile-provisioning.md

docs/contracts/decisions/Q6-profile-provisioning.md::rationale

Rationale

Rationale

Industry patterns for capability provisioning:

| Approach | Examples | Trade-off | |----------|----------|-----------| | Static manifest | Cargo.toml, package.json, go.mod, Python requirements.txt | Explicit, auditable, reproducible, reviewable | | Dynamic query | npm workspaces, Bazel labels, Nix flakes | Flexible, but opaque; "what skills does this profile have?" requires running code | | Hybrid | Poetry groups, Cargo features | Best of both: static manifest with optional dynamic composition |

Static manifests win for auditability and reproducibility. A human (or CI) can read .agent/profiles/conceptualizer.md and know exactly which skills are provisioned without executing code. This is critical for: - Security review: "Does this profile have the shell skill?" - Reproducibility: Same commit → same active skill set - Debugging: "Why does this profile have skill X?" → check frontmatter, not query logic

The dynamic fallback (--dynamic) supports development exploration (e.g., "give me all task_type=planning skills") but does not replace the committed manifest.

docs/integration/harness-contract.md::harness-adapter-contract

Harness-Adapter Contract

Harness-Adapter Contract

contract_version: 1.0.0

This document specifies the file-based integration surface between the WorkspaceAlpha baselayer and any harness that consumes it. The contract is versioned using semver; breaking changes require a major version bump.

docs/integration/harness-contract.md::read-order

Read Order

Read Order

A harness must consume workspace artifacts in this order:

1. AGENTS.md — Agent router entry point (≤150 lines). Read first for orientation. 2. .context/manifest.json — Generated routing table. Contains node IDs, byte ranges, SHA-256 hashes, and edges. Defines the DAG structure. 3. .harness/skills/ — Currently-used skill set, provisioned per active profile via python3 .harness/sync_active.py --profile <name>.

Do NOT read docs/ directly. Do NOT grep for content in docs. Hydrate sections only by byte_range from manifest.json.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/integration/harness-contract.md

docs/integration/harness-contract.md::invariants

Invariants

Invariants

A harness may assume the following are always true:

| Invariant | Description | |-----------|-------------| | Manifest is acyclic | No cycles in the DAG (validated by build.py and validate.py) | | Node IDs are unique | No duplicate IDs in manifest.json | | Byte ranges are valid | byte_range[0] < byte_range[1] and within file bounds | | SHA-256 hashes match | Each node's hash matches the content at its byte range | | Active skills ⊆ provisioned skills | Every skill in .harness/skills/ exists in .agent/skills/ | | Contract version present | manifest.json contains contract_version field | | AGENTS.md ≤ 150 lines | Router stays under ~15% of context budget |

docs/integration/harness-contract.md::what-a-harness-may-assume

What a Harness May Assume

What a Harness May Assume

- manifest.json is regenerated by python3 .wiki/build.py after any docs change - .context/graph.json is the source of truth; manifest is derived - .wiki/index.html is the human-readable rendering of the same graph - Skill frontmatter in .agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is authoritative for skill metadata - Profile frontmatter in .agent/profiles/<name>.md determines which skills are active - validate.py passes on every commit (pre-commit hook)

docs/integration/harness-contract.md::what-a-harness-must-not-assume

What a Harness Must NOT Assume

What a Harness Must NOT Assume

- Do not grep docs/ directly. Use manifest.json byte ranges instead. - Do not read .wiki/index.html for programmatic decisions. It's for humans. - Do not assume skill files have a particular structure beyond frontmatter. Body format varies. - Do not assume .agent/ is untracked. It may or may not be in git depending on deployment model. - Do not assume network access. All tools are stdlib-only; no external API calls. - Do not assume .env contains real keys. It's gitignored and may be empty.

docs/operations/secrets.md::rotation-procedure

Rotation Procedure

Rotation Procedure

When a key needs rotation (compromise, expiration, scheduled refresh):

1. Revoke the old key with the provider (e.g., Exa dashboard for EXA_API_KEY) 2. Issue a new key from the provider 3. Update .agent/.env with the new value 4. Restart the harness / any long-running process using the key

No restart of the build pipeline or wiki renderer is required — keys are read at runtime by individual skills.

doc docs/operations/secrets.md

docs/operations/secrets.md::key-leak-response

Key Leak Response

Key Leak Response

If a real credential is accidentally committed to git:

1. Revoke immediately — assume the key is compromised 2. Rotate — issue a new key, update .agent/.env 3. Purge history — use git filter-branch or bfg to remove the key from all commits 4. Verify — git log --all -p should return no real credential values in tracked files

docs/resources/README.md::resources-skills-archive-provenance

Resources — Skills Archive Provenance

Resources — Skills Archive Provenance

Archive status: the raw dump (.archive/Agentsandskills/, 686M, 3,510 sources) was imported into .agent/skills/ — 3,463 copied as valid folders, 47 "404: Not Found" sources quarantined (see .agent/skills/IMPORT_REPORT.md), indexed in .agent/skills/INDEX.md + INDEX.csv (3,520 folders). The archive was cleared after verification; workspace shrank 689M → 157M. The dump itself was never baselayer-indexed.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/resources/README.md

docs/resources/README.md::provenance

Provenance

Provenance

The dump aggregates 13 buckets (see .archive/Agentsandskills/agent.md and .archive/Agentsandskills/AgentSkills/DATABASE.md for the full inventory, which is stale — counts disagree across files, by-source/ lists only 6 of 13 buckets, harness-skills-names.txt lists 28 of 60 installed). Every SKILL.md keeps original frontmatter; nothing here is rewritten. (The dump's OVERLAPS/INSTALLATION/DATABASE files are no longer present post-clear; treat as historical notes.)

Why is the dump not indexed?

- 136M of 150M is dump/agentic-awesome-skills (2,947 skills), with uniform frontmatter but no per-skill quality signal. Auto-ingesting it would swamp the router (3,509 nodes, most low-signal) and break the 150-line AGENTS.md token budget. - Bulk install is prohibited by OVERLAPS.md / INSTALLATION.md. Install one skill at a time, diff it first. - Trust spread: security-offensive skills (active-directory-attacks, windows-privilege-escalation, apk-reverse, XSS, api-fuzzing) carry risk: offensive/critical and impose their own confirmation gates. Never auto-install security skills, x402 (USDC payments, installed copy included), or any skill with executable scripts/ without review — scripts ship unsigned. - License field is inconsistent (MIT in some, absent in others); external GitHub URL dependencies exist (e.g. aws-skills router).

Integrity findings

- 3 installed skills are broken at source (SKILL.md = "404: Not Found" in both .harness/skills and dump/): caveman, karpathy-coder, llm-cost-optimizer. Excluded from the workspace copy (57, not 60). - caveman, karpathy-coder, llm-cost-optimizer names collide with healthy skills elsewhere (dump/ponytail has a real caveman pack; andrej-karpathy is the healthy Karpathy skill) — check OVERLAPS.md before installing any dump copy. - agent.md count claims (60 vs 28 vs 27 installed, 3,405 vs 3,413 vs 3,509 total, 14 sources for 13 buckets) are mutually inconsistent. Treat DATABASE.md/INDEX.csv as approximate; verify on disk.

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::overview

Overview

Overview

This document specifies the persistence layer for audit logging in the Baselayer workspace. It defines how audit records are stored, queried, and retained across sessions.

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::requirements

Requirements

Requirements

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::functional-requirements

Functional Requirements

Functional Requirements

1. Immutable Audit Trail: Once written, audit records cannot be modified or deleted 2. Queryable: Support filtering by timestamp, agent, task, outcome, and tags 3. Partitioned: Store by date (YYYY-MM-DD) for efficient time-range queries 4. Compressed: Use efficient binary format for long-term storage 5. Replicable: Support export/import for backup and migration

requires
none
required by
none
doc docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::non-functional-requirements

Non-Functional Requirements

Non-Functional Requirements

| Requirement | Target | |-------------|--------| | Write latency (p99) | < 10ms | | Read latency (p99) | < 50ms for 10k records | | Storage overhead | < 20% vs raw JSONL | | Retention | Configurable, default 90 days | | Durability | fsync on each write |

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::primary-sqlite-with-fts5

Primary: SQLite with FTS5

Primary: SQLite with FTS5

- Table: audit_log with columns matching data model - FTS5 virtual table for full-text search on task, tags, context_ref - Indexes on timestamp, agent, outcome - WAL mode for concurrent reads during writes

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::write-path

Write Path

Write Path

1. Agent emits record via knowledge.py add --kind work 2. knowledge.py sync writes to SQLite + JSONL atomically 3. Background job compresses JSONL older than 7 days 4. Retention job deletes partitions older than configured TTL

required by

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::read-path

Read Path

Read Path

1. knowledge.py search <query> → FTS5 query 2. knowledge.py last --kind work -n 5 → indexed timestamp query 3. Export: knowledge.py export --since YYYY-MM-DD --format jsonl

Access Control

Access Control

- Only the active agent session may write - Read access via knowledge tool (no direct DB access) - Export requires explicit human approval (ESCALATION protocol)

audit:
  retention_days: 90
  compression_after_days: 7
  sqlite_path: ".context/audit.db"
  jsonl_dir: "memory/runs"
  wal_mode: true
  sync_on_write: true

docs/specs/audit-persistence-spec.md::migration-strategy

Migration Strategy

Migration Strategy

- Version field in each record enables schema evolution - knowledge.py migrate --to-version N handles upgrades - Backward compatibility: readers handle missing fields gracefully - No downgrade support (immutable trail)

Testing

Testing

- Property-based tests: write N records, verify all readable - Chaos tests: kill process mid-write, verify no corruption - Performance benchmarks: CI gate on latency targets - Retention integration test: verify TTL cleanup
